Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral, symmetric hilar lymph node enlargement with well-defined margins and clear lung fields, which is the classic radiographic presentation of Stage I sarcoidosis. This symmetric pattern helps distinguish it from malignancy (often asymmetric) or tuberculosis (often unilateral), while the absence of pulmonary opacities rules out Stage II/III disease or active infection.
